title: GPU occupancy vs interconnect gradients - lab log
body:
Purpose:
This is a running lab notebook for an experiment series investigating how GPU occupancy interacts with interconnect behavior (NVLink vs PCIe), NCCL handoff timing, and prefetch windows for multi-GPU LLM inference. Goal is to find practical knobs (prefetch depth, KV cache staging placement, NCCL scheduling hints) that improve p50/p95 generation latency without sacrificing throughput or quality.

Background / motivation:
- Recent production traces show occasional p95 spikes when request mix shifts to many short-context queries. Hypothesis: brief compute stalls leave GPUs under-occupied and cause jitter in NCCL collective scheduling, amplifying interconnect contention (microbursts) and host staging variations.
- Prior notes focused on long-run bandwidth saturation; this work looks at transient occupancy gradients across a step-up in arrival rate and interplay with prefetch window sizing (how many future layers we prefetch weights/KV into GPU memory).

Setup (hardware/software):
- Testbed: 1 rack node with 8x A100-40GB (DGX-like), two NICs for load gen separation. Topology: pairwise NVLink rings in groups of 4, x16 PCIe links to host.
- SW: custom inference harness (repo: repo/serving-runtime/infer-harness), runtime build: bench/opt-2025-01, NCCL v2.18, CUDA 11.8, driver 535.xx.
- Models: distilled-13B baseline and open-70B quantized 4-bit variant used sparingly. Sequence lengths: 32 short, 2048 long. Mixed request mix: 70% short, 30% long.
- Instrumentation: per-GPU occupancy counters (nsys/nsight), nvlink util telemetry via nvidia-smi dmon + on-card perf counters, host kernel tracing (ftrace) for PCIe page faults, NCCL debug logs set to level 4, and a lightweight packet-capture for NVLink (vendor telemetry). Also added timestamped KV-cache prefetch markers in the harness.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Vary prefetch window depth: 0 (no prefetch), 1, 4, 8 layers ahead.
- Replica placement: colocated (all shards in same NVLink island) vs distributed (shards spread across islands).
- NCCL scheduling parameter tweaks: NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS=1 vs 0, and NCCL_P2P_LEVEL adjusting p2p fallback thresholds.
- Host staging policy: immediate mmap-on-demand vs eager pinned staging.

Quick observations (raw):
- No-prefetch (0): highest p50 for short requests but surprisingly lower p95 jitter in some distributed placements. Explanation hypothesis: when no prefetch, per-layer compute follows memory access strictly — NCCL collectives are aligned with compute, creating smaller, more regular packets.
- Prefetch=4: Best aggregate throughput for long sequences but introduced microburst NVLink usage peaks when short requests interleave, causing 15-22% p95 increases for short requests in distributed shard placement.
- Prefetch=1: Sweet spot in several runs; reduced layer-to-layer occupancy swings without generating large simultaneous NVLink transfers. Gave 6-9% p95 improvement vs no-prefetch in colocated placement for our short-heavy mix.
- Eager pinned staging reduced host->GPU latency variance but increased average PCIe utilization; combined with Prefetch=8 this led to persistent link saturation and tail events.

Representative trace excerpts (high-level):
- Trace A (prefetch=4, distributed, NCCL_ASYNC=0): compute utilization per GPU oscillates between 62% and 95% in 5ms windows during bursty short-query periods. NVLink telemetry shows 3x peaks concurrent with layer boundary handoffs, correlating with 40-60us increases in allreduce completion times.
- Trace B (prefetch=1, colocated, NCCL_ASYNC=1): occupancy steadier at 88±6%, NVLink peaks smoothed, avg allreduce latency dropped by 18% and p95 generation latency for short requests improved by 8%.

Metrics table (summary numbers from a representative run):
- Config: Prefetch=1, Colocated, NCCL_ASYNC=1, eager staging=off -> throughput: 1.00x baseline, p50 short: 12ms (-7%), p95 short: 48ms (-8%), NVLink 95th-percentile per-link BW: 64GB/s.
- Config: Prefetch=4, Distributed, NCCL_ASYNC=0, eager staging=on -> throughput: 1.12x baseline (long seqs), p50 short: 14ms (+5%), p95 short: 65ms (+22%), NVLink 95th-per-link: 92GB/s, PCIe stall counts +18%.

Interpretation and hypotheses refined:
1) Over-aggressive prefetching aligns many GPUs to perform memory-bound work at the same microsecond boundaries; this creates NVLink microbursts which the interconnect scheduling handles poorly when occupancy is low/variable.
2) Slightly conservative prefetch depth (1-2 layers) acts as a dampener, decoupling exact layer boundaries across replicas and smoothing out collective timings.
3) NCCL async progress helps when combined with colocated shards because it allows background progression of collectives when CPU scheduling introduces jitter. When shards are distributed, async progress can also worsen contention unless the prefetch window is tuned.

Immediate actionable mitigations to try in prod-like config:
- Make default prefetch window adaptive: start at 1 layer, increase to 4 only when sustained per-GPU occupancy > 80% for 500ms.
- Prefer colocated shard placement for latency-sensitive, short-heavy workloads; document tradeoffs for throughput on long sequences.
- Enable NCCL_ASYNC_PROGRESS by default for colocated placements and only when host CPU utilization < 60%.
- Add micro-batching jitter: small random offset (0-2ms) before launching a prefetched collective to desynchronize replicas when prefetch>1.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Verify behavior on H100 (different NVLink fabric/latency characteristics). Plan: replicate key runs on H100 dev nodes week of 2025-02-10.
- Evaluate impact on quality/regression tests for inference with prefetch jitter (ensure deterministic ordering where needed).
- Probe NIC interrupts and kernel scheduling interplay further: does IRQ affinity correlate with observed latency spikes? Add perf top + irq affinity sweep.
- Try NCCL tuning knob NCCL_ALGO=RING_TREE and measure effect on p95 for distributed shards.

Notes for reproducibility (how to run a similar experiment):
1) Checkout repo/serving-runtime at commit b3f4a9c.
2) Build harness with BENCH_MODE=multi-gpu-occupancy and enable KV prefetch tracing.
3) Use loadgen script experiments/short_long_mix.yml with seed=20250118.
4) Collect traces with nsys --sample=nvtx and capture NCCL logs to /tmp/nccl-log-*.
5) Post-process with scripts/perf/strip-and-aggregate.py to extract layer boundaries and NVLink burst histograms.

Appendix - random observations and raw notes:
- Observed a weird case where one GPU would transiently drop to 20% occupancy for ~120ms after a 2k-long request finish; root cause looked like page reclaim on host due to pinned staging combined with a kernel memory pressure path. Filed JIRA SRV-2231.
- For the 70B quantized runs, prefetch=8 was mandatory to avoid page thrash, but required colocated islands to keep tail latency acceptable.
- Linear backoff for prefetch depth (increase by 1 per sustained 200ms occupancy >90%) performed worse than hysteresis+threshold approach.

Next experiments (ordered):
- Param sweep: prefetch depths {0,1,2,4,8} x shard placement {colocated, distributed} x NCCL_ASYNC {0,1} — capture 1000 short requests steady-state and analyze p99.
- H100 replication.
- Microbatch jitter magnitude sweep {0,0.5ms,1ms,2ms,5ms}.

Conclusions (interim):
- The system's tail latency for short requests is sensitive to how tightly layer compute is synchronized across GPUs. Prefetch is a powerful lever that trades throughput for synchronization; modest prefetch combined with async NCCL progress and placement-aware policies provides the best latency/throughput balance for mixed workloads.
